title: Credentialed Shadow Enforcer for Graduated Batching & KV-Cache Rollouts
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Optimize suggestions (batch size, prefix caching, KV cache retention) can yield large cost savings but introduce regressions in latency, tail QPS behavior, or model output quality. We need an automated enforcer that can safely apply recommendations while providing operator controls and automatic rollback when telemetry indicates risk.

Goal: Implement a credentialed ‘shadow enforcer’ service that performs graduated, shadowed rollouts of Optimize recommendations under an operator-escrowed approval model. The service must support traffic shadowing, percentage-based graduated activation windows, telemetry-driven kill-switches, and a minimal human-acknowledge approval flow for high-impact changes.

Non-goals: Full built-in simulation of all customer workloads (we will rely on configurable synthetic canaries); replacing existing rollout orchestration frameworks (we integrate with rollout-controller APIs).
acceptance_criteria: Credentialed enforcer can accept an Optimize suggestion bundle and create a shadowed rollout plan that does not affect production traffic unless explicitly promoted
Graduated activation supports steps: 0% shadow -> 1% dark traffic -> 5% routed -> 25% routed -> 100% routed, with configurable dwell times
Telemetry sentinel rules fire and trigger automated rollback within SLA when latency P95 increases > 15% or error rate delta > 0.5% or eval-set text-quality degradation > defined threshold
Operator approval workflow (escrow token) required for >5% routed traffic changes; approval events are auditable in the console and emitted to audit logs
Rollback playbook executes deterministic revert and annotates the associated suggestion and rollout with reason and diagnostics
End-to-end E2E test harness demonstrates a safe rollback in response to synthetic latency spike within a CI job
technical_notes: We will implement the enforcer as a stateless controller with a small credential store for operator escrow tokens (KMS-backed) and time-limited JWTs for actioning promotions
Shadowing: use existing request-proxy to fork 100% of candidate requests to a mirrored execution path; mirrored responses are recorded for diffing but not used in real responses
Routing: integrate with rollout-controller API to programmatically change weights; maintain an internal ledger of active plans for auditing and for crash-safe resumption
Telemetry: reuse metric collectors from console (latency, token cost, errors) plus a lightweight eval-runner that scores synthetic prompts against golden outputs for quality drift detection
Safety leash: implement two-tier thresholds: 'soft' which emits warnings and pauses promotion, and 'hard' which automatically reverts (configurable per-customer and per-model)
Operator friction: require an operator-escrow step (human in the loop) if estimated monthly cost delta > $5000 or >5% user-visible latency impact
Revert: rollout-controller revert + optimizer snapshot restore; annotate commit in model-config-store and attach telemetry snapshot for postmortem
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Intake: Suggestion arrives with metadata (estimated cost delta, affected routes). Validate suggestion schema and run static checks (config ranges)
Phase 1 - Shadow run: Mirror requests for 72 hours, collect latencies, errors, and synthesized quality scores; require >=90% pass rate on eval-set before promotion
Phase 2 - Gradual routing: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with configurable dwell (default 2h, override allowed for low-impact changes)
Phase 3 - Operator escrow: For steps that increase routed traffic beyond 5% or cost delta beyond threshold, surface approval request in Console; wait for a credentialed operator token
Phase 4 - Monitor & enforce: Telemetry sent to enforcer sentinel; on hard threshold breach, automatically revert and notify Ops
Phase 5 - Postmortem & learning: Persist telemetry snapshots and diff artifacts; attach to suggestion and optionally trigger a regression alert in Optimize
test_plan: Unit tests for enforcer state machine and token expiry semantics
Integration tests: simulate suggestion intake -> shadow -> routing -> revert using staging rollout-controller and synthetic traffic generator
Chaos test: inject latency spikes in shadowed backend and assert automatic rollback within configured SLA
Security test: verify escrow tokens are KMS-encrypted and revoke path works; run a small pen-test on controller endpoints
Cost regression test: validate cost-estimate calculations against historical billing dataset (sampled customers)
